upstream.proposal:
Fix option source masking when source is unknown (aka undefined)

## Problem

A global option value with an unknown source fails to mask the leaf option value source in `.getOptionValueSourceWithGlobals()`

Fixes: #2651

## Solution

Unlikely to happen in practice, but is not as intended and a simple code change.

Test for presence of option value source, rather than value of option value source.

## ChangeLog

- fix: global option values with unknown source should mask local option value source in  `.getOptionValueSourceWithGlobals()`

evidence.contract: packet/C.patch handles setter-created unknown sources: starting lib/command.js setOptionValue delegates to setOptionValueWithSource, which creates a source entry even for undefined. Frozen build/native/contract/preserve checks all exit 0. However, checking only _optionValueSources misses values represented by opts() without an entry. Static counterexample: p = new Command().storeOptionsAsProperties().option("--common <value>"); s = p.command("sub").option("--common <value>"); p.common = "parent"; s.setOptionValueWithSource("common", "child", "cli"). opts() includes p.common, so s.optsWithGlobals().common is "parent", but C returns "cli" for its source instead of undefined. This follows from opts(), the setters and the changed condition; it was not executed.
evidence.tests: packet/C.patch adds a meaningful CLI regression using setOptionValueWithSource with omitted source, distinguishing the starting defect. It retains the original global-default assertion under a clearer name and deletes no protection. Added coverage omits unknown values without source entries, legacy storage, undefined values and nested unknown-source precedence. Existing nesting tests exercise merged values rather than this source interaction.
evidence.design: The own-source-entry check is minimal and fits the internal map and setter behavior. Its avoidable limitation is substituting source-map ownership for the value ownership used by optsWithGlobals(), leaving legacy property storage inconsistent. No unrelated edits or validation bypasses are present.
evidence.proposal: packet/C.md accurately names the defect and explains the source-presence implementation. It reports no verification or limitations and does not explain preserved behavior or coverage. This is an observed communication omission, not unavailable historical text. Frozen passing checks are assessed separately from the proposal.

evidence.contract: packet/B.patch fixes explicitly undefined entries made by setOptionValueWithSource or setOptionValue: starting lib/command.js records a source-map key for either setter. Frozen build/native/contract/preserve exits are 0. A value-ownership edge remains: create parent = new Command().storeOptionsAsProperties(true).option("--common <value>"), set parent.common = "parent", create child = parent.command("sub"), and call child.setOptionValueWithSource("common", "child", "cli"). optsWithGlobals returns parent, but B returns cli because the parent has no source-map key. Leaving parent.common undefined also produces a mismatch. This follows mechanically from starting opts(), the setters and B's predicate; tests/options.opts.test.js establishes declared undefined property keys.
evidence.tests: packet/B.patch adds one meaningful CLI regression in tests/options.optsWithGlobals.test.js using a parent value set with an omitted source, and clarifies an existing default-source test name without weakening its assertion. It omits the distinct property-storage path with an opts-owned key and no source entry, nesting, undefined values and broader recognized-source coverage. Frozen native success covers the reported focused slice.
evidence.design: The one-line Object.hasOwn(_optionValueSources, key) change is small and fits source-map bookkeeping, with no unrelated edits. However, it couples masking to source-entry ownership rather than the value ownership used by optsWithGlobals, leaving the concrete compatibility edge described under contract. No existing validation or protection is removed.
evidence.proposal: packet/B.md gives a precise title, explains the defect and accurately describes checking source-entry presence. It omits verification results and limitations and does not explain the value/source ownership boundary. Frozen checks are assessed separately and do not supply missing proposal content.

evidence.contract: packet/A.patch changes lib/command.js:getOptionValueSourceWithGlobals to require an own _optionValueSources entry. setOptionValueWithSource writes such an entry even for undefined, so the added CLI regression is repaired; packet/task.json records build, native, contract and preserve exit 0. A material boundary remains: with a parent using storeOptionsAsProperties().option("--common <value>"), assign parent.common = "parent" and set the child common value/source to "child"/"cli". Starting opts() reads the parent property and optsWithGlobals() returns "parent", but A skips the parent because no source entry exists and returns "cli". This follows mechanically from lib/command.js:944-950, 977 and 1914-1939; it was not executed.
evidence.tests: packet/A.patch adds one discriminating test in tests/options.optsWithGlobals.test.js: a parent setOptionValueWithSource call with omitted source must mask a child CLI source. It retains the existing default-global and child-only assertions and only clarifies one test name. It does not add nesting, property storage, undefined-value, or value-without-source-entry coverage. Frozen native exit is 0.
evidence.design: The one-line own-property check is small and correctly distinguishes an explicitly stored undefined source from an absent source. However, using only _optionValueSources as the ownership authority does not fully match optsWithGlobals, which merges cmd.opts(); property-backed or directly populated option values can exist without source entries. No unrelated production changes or weakened protections appear in the full patch.
evidence.proposal: packet/A.md precisely identifies unknown-source masking and explains the source-presence implementation. It makes no unsupported check claims, but supplies no verification account or limitations and describes the narrower source-entry approach rather than the full value-precedence boundary.
